hints: Because the plane is smooth and the system is released from rest, total mechanical energy is conserved: $\text{Gain in KE} = \text{Net loss in PE}$.
Express the total gain in kinetic energy for both particles moving with common speed $v$: $\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}(m_A + m_B)v^2 = \frac{1}{2}(0.8 + 1.6)v^2$.
Calculate the loss in PE of hanging particle $B$ falling $0.5\text{ m}$: $\Delta E_{p,B} = m_B g d = 1.6(10)(0.5)$.

Calculate the gain in PE of particle $A$ moving $0.5\text{ m}$ up the incline: $\Delta E_{p,A} = m_A g(d\sin\theta) = 0.8(10)(0.5)(0.6)$, then equate $\Delta E_k = \Delta E_{p,B} - \Delta E_{p,A}$ and solve for $v$.
walkthrough:
Express the total kinetic energy gained by particles $A$ and $B$ from rest:
$$\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}m_A v^2 + \frac{1}{2}m_B v^2 = \frac{1}{2}(0.8 + 1.6)v^2 = 1.2v^2$$

Calculate the potential energy changes when each particle moves distance $d = 0.5\text{ m}$:
$$\text{Loss in PE of } B: \quad \Delta E_{p,B} = m_B g d = 1.6(10)(0.5) = 8\text{ J}$$
$$\text{Gain in PE of } A: \quad \Delta E_{p,A} = m_A g(d\sin\theta) = 0.8(10)(0.5)(0.6) = 2.4\text{ J}$$

Equate the total kinetic energy gain to the net potential energy loss:
$$\Delta E_k = \Delta E_{p,B} - \Delta E_{p,A}$$
$$1.2v^2 = 8 - 2.4 = 5.6$$

Solve for the speed $v$:
$$v^2 = \frac{5.6}{1.2} = \frac{14}{3} \approx 4.6667$$
$$v = \sqrt{\frac{14}{3}} \approx 2.1602 \approx 2.16\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the principle of conservation of mechanical energy for a system with no non-conservative work (smooth surfaces, light inextensible string):
$$\Delta E_k = -\Delta E_p$$
$$\text{Gain in Kinetic Energy} = \text{Net Loss in Gravitational Potential Energy}$$

Calculate the kinetic energy gained by the two connected particles starting from rest ($u = 0$):
$$\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}(m_A + m_B)v^2$$
Substitute $m_A = 0.8\text{ kg}$ and $m_B = 1.6\text{ kg}$:
$$\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}(0.8 + 1.6)v^2 = \frac{1}{2}(2.4)v^2 = 1.2v^2$$

Calculate the gravitational potential energy lost by particle $B$ descending vertically by $h_B = 0.5\text{ m}$:
$$\Delta E_{p,B} = m_B g h_B = 1.6 \times 10 \times 0.5 = 8\text{ J}$$

Calculate the gravitational potential energy gained by particle $A$ moving distance $d = 0.5\text{ m}$ up the plane of inclination $\sin\theta = 0.6$:
$$\text{Vertical rise of } A: \quad h_A = d\sin\theta = 0.5 \times 0.6 = 0.3\text{ m}$$
$$\Delta E_{p,A} = m_A g h_A = 0.8 \times 10 \times 0.3 = 2.4\text{ J}$$

Compute the net loss in gravitational potential energy:
$$\Delta E_{p,\text{net loss}} = 8 - 2.4 = 5.6\text{ J}$$

Equate the kinetic energy gain to the net potential energy loss:
$$1.2v^2 = 5.6$$
Divide both sides by $1.2$:
$$v^2 = \frac{5.6}{1.2} = \frac{56}{12} = \frac{14}{3}$$
Take the positive square root:
$$v = \sqrt{\frac{14}{3}} \approx 2.16025 \approx 2.16\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.Applying the Work\u2013Energy Principle: Equates $\text{Gain in KE} = 1.2v^2$ to $\text{Loss in PE} = 8 - 2.4 = 5.6$ and solves for $v = 2.16\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
